all_of: the client holds a cookie or parameter that decodes to a serialized object graph rather than to plain data
the value is accepted without a signature or message authentication code
any_of: the decoded bytes contain readable module and class names alongside single-letter opcodes
a value derived from the deserialized object is rendered back into the response

chain.action: decode every opaque cookie and read the bytes as text before treating the value as opaque
chain.why: the lowest pickle protocol is printable ASCII, so the format, the class names and the fact that the server deserializes it are all visible without tooling

chain.action: follow the request through and check whether anything derived from the deserialized object appears in the response
chain.why: a rendered value turns the bug into a direct output channel, which removes any need for a callback host, a timing oracle or an outbound connection

chain.action: hand-write the serialized payload in the lowest protocol, replacing the object's value with a call to a subprocess helper that returns its output
chain.why: generating the payload from a newer interpreter emits opcodes and module paths the target cannot resolve, so the portable route is to write the opcodes directly

chain.action: run a harmless marker command first and look for its exact output in the rendered position
chain.why: the marker proves execution while changing nothing, which is what makes the confirmation safe to run on a shared instance

chain.action: swap the argument vector for a shell invocation, list the application directory, and read the file whose name does not belong to the framework
chain.why: the output channel returns command output inline, so locating and reading the objective costs two requests

first_confirming_probe.request: replace the deserialized value with a call that returns the output of a harmless marker command, and request the page that renders it
first_confirming_probe.expected: the marker's exact output appears in the position where the object was previously printed
first_confirming_probe.falsifier: the response is unchanged, an error page is returned, or the value is rejected because it carries no valid signature

blast_radius: this is command execution on the challenge container, and here that container runs as root. Keep every command read-only, such as listing a directory or printing a file. Never write, delete or restart anything: a single careless command can brick the instance for every player. Confirm with a marker that only prints, and read the objective with one further command.

verification.evidence: the flag was rendered inline in the page returned by the live target, in the same element that previously printed the deserialized object

reuse_when: a cookie decodes to something containing module or class names rather than to plain data
an application on an older interpreter round-trips state through the client with no integrity check
the deserialized value is echoed, printed or rendered anywhere in the response
known_traps: generating the payload with a newer interpreter than the target emits string opcodes and module paths the target cannot resolve; write the opcodes by hand in the lowest protocol instead
the class named in the default cookie is usually decorative and carries no behaviour, so time spent reconstructing it is wasted; the value simply has to be replaced
the deserialization happens before any route logic when it is wired into a pre-request handler, so every path on the site carries the primitive, not only the one that renders it
